Subject: ACMEHealth — Private VPC data flow review & follow-up

Hi Emily / James,

Thanks again for taking the time today — great conversation. Per our discovery, here is a short recap of where we landed and the proposed next steps so we can validate constraints for a Private (VPC) deployment: 

Summary of needs:
- PII classification: PHI/PCI-level data may be passed to the model during inference; strong need to control egress and logging.
- Data residency: primary data residency in US (east), but some customers are EU-based — will need options for region-specific deployment.
- Logging & retention: Acme requires audit logs for all inference requests, with retention control and ability to disable application-level request logging for specific routes.
- Network controls: traffic must be within a customer VPC with strict egress rules; approved outbound endpoints only; option for air-gapped/on-prem for extremely sensitive workloads.

Immediate next steps (proposed):
1) Share a draft VPC dataflow diagram (attached) and a short tech sheet describing Private deployment modes.
2) Rishi to confirm egress controls, logging knobs, and SOC2 evidence we can surface.
3) Set up a technical follow-up with your network/security team — proposed times Wed/Thu this week.

Attachments: vpc-dataflow-draft.pdf (diagram)

If any of the above is incorrect or missing items, please flag and we'll update. I'll loop Rishi and Monica into the follow-up.

Best,

Marissa,

Thanks for the recap — looks good overall. A few clarifying Qs from our Security & Privacy folks: 

1) Can you confirm whether Redwood’s Private deployment supports disabling request/response logging at the tenant/route level? We need to make sure PHI is never persisted in logs for certain endpoints.
2) What are the available egress control mechanisms? Specifically, can we restrict outbound traffic to only our NAT + specific IP ranges, and disallow DNS-based egress?
3) For customers requiring EU residency, do you provide region-pinned control plane and inference nodes?
4) We will need SOC 2 Type II evidence and a list of sub-processors. Can you send those artifacts or a path to obtain them?

Also, James flagged that a fully air-gapped/on-prem option may be required for one of our pilot customers — is there precedent for an on-prem air-gapped deployment?

Happy to do a tech call Wed 10:30am PT if that works for your team.

Emily — thanks, good questions. Looping in Rishi (SE) and Monica (CS) to address the tech and compliance pieces. Quick answers while we prep artifacts: 

- Logging/retention: Redwood Private supports per-tenant and per-route logging controls. We can disable request/response persistence and filter sensitive fields before logs are written. We also offer a configurable retention window (customer-controlled).
- Egress controls: VPC deployments support strict egress policies via security groups and VPC route tables; outbound traffic can be restricted to specific NAT IPs and CIDR ranges. We also support disabling DNS resolution in the runtime and forcing egress through an approved proxy.
- Region pinning: Yes — we can deploy inference nodes in region-specific pools (US-EAST, EU-WEST). The control plane can be hosted in a customer VPC or in a region-locked private control plane depending on the contract.
- Compliance artifacts: we'll surface SOC 2 Type II report and sub-processor list — Monica will share the access path.
- Air-gapped/on-prem: Rishi, can you confirm feasibility and what that engagement looks like?

We can do Wed 10:30am PT — I'll send a calendar invite once Rishi confirms.

Thanks,
Marissa

Hi Emily / James / Marissa —

Quick tech note ahead of the call and attaching a short deployment sheet. High-level answers: 

1) Logging controls:
- Per-route/tenant logging: supported. We offer filtering at the SDK/sidecar layer to strip or mask sensitive fields before any log emission. For extreme cases we can run with logging disabled for specified routes.
- Audit logs: all management actions and orchestration events can be sent to your SIEM (via syslog/CloudWatch/Stackdriver) and stored for your retention policy.

2) Egress controls:
- Egress is enforced via customer VPC route tables + security-group ACLs; deployment nodes have no default internet route.
- You can restrict outbound to only your NAT IPs and approved CIDRs.
- DNS hardening: we support forcing DNS resolution to an internal resolver and/or disabling external resolution; we can also route all egress through a proxy appliance you control.

3) Region & residency:
- We support region-pinned inference pools and can provision dedicated nodes in EU-WEST for EU-residency customers.

4) Air-gapped/on-prem:
- We have executed on-prem, air-gapped customers. Typical engagement includes an initial scoping week, packaging a runtime container with offline installers, and an on-site validation + runbook handover. Timeline: ~8-12 weeks depending on approval windows and networking readiness.

Attachment: redwood_private_vpc_deployment_sheet.pdf (3 pages)

I'll be prepared to demo the sidecar masking and routing controls on the call.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
